answer: The strongest lever is simple: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because sonnet only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, vault is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any velvet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
